summary: Shoku Bando is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University (MA), and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held posts at Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Warder, Venkatacharya, and Matilal, among others. He was Professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Otani University (~1928–1931) and Horyuji Kangakuin under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki. He held posts at Otani University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He held several posts at Taisho University, including Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014).

Shoshin Kuwayama works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966), where he served as Assistant Professor (~1978–1989) and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities (~1966–2002).

Shoshun Hayashidera works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and serves as a Professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, University of Tokyo, and University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1928–1954), Komazawa University (~1954–1973), Toyo University, and Waseda University (~1959–1964).

Shou-chien Shih specializes in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He was a PhD student at National Sun Yat-sen University, served as Professor at National Taiwan University (~1987–2000), and was director at the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004).

Shozen Kumoi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He taught at Otani University (1948–1981; Emeritus ~1986–2017) and held posts at Kyoto and Bukkyo universities.
Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as a Professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar who taught Dieter Schuh. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. He held posts as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College, and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (~1888–1893).
Shridhar Tryambak Pathak was an Indologist. He served as Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and served as Professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (1981–2009), Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Sri Narayana Mishra specialized in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, having studied under Anantalal Thakur. He served at Banaras Hindu University as Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1971), Reader (attested 1985), and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1915–1927) and Secretary and Mahabharata General Editor at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University and held an affiliation with the Vrindaban Research Institute (attested 1994).

Shu-chen Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at the University of Virginia, completing her PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

Shu-fen Chen is a linguistics and Indology scholar. She studied at National Tsing Hua University and completed doctoral studies under Hans Henrich Hock, later serving as Professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held a post as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).
